messages:
Maya: quick async - proposing a 'preflight-first' flow for private deploy upgrades so customers can sign-off IP reservations through our export + webhook. Core idea: generate a manifest, present an approval URL that maps to a short-lived signed token, and only proceed once firewall owner acknowledges. Goals: reduce upgrade rejections and make contract SLAs actionable.

Priya: +1 from field. A lot of customers refuse upgrades because firewall ops want an auditable ok. If we surface an approval URL and record who clicked it (SAML identity), that should satisfy change control. Need to include contact info and expected outage window.

Victor: implementation notes: exporter will emit manifest.json + manifest.sig. New endpoint /api/v1/manifests/{id}/approve returns a signed token when the approver authenticates. Installer then consumes token during cutover: 
```bash
./installer apply --manifest-token=ey... --profile=vpc-reserved
```
If token absent or expired, upgrade pauses and logs an event.

Linh: also add a dry-run validator that runs smoke tests using the proposed egress IPs. We should surface a "confidence" score for tenant-nat predictions. For vpc-reserved, confidence = 100% if IPs are statically allocated.

security: must enforce envelope encryption for manifests and require customer CMK binding for signing OR require our HSM with customer-owned keys. Approval URL must be single-use, timeboxed, require mfa, and produce an immutable audit event: who, when, ip, request-id. Add retention spec: audit events retained 90d by default, configurable in enterprise contracts.

Maya: legal asks: can we include an appendix that defines SLA terms tied to the approval flow? e.g., "if customer provides signed approval token >=24h before cutover, Redwood guarantees egress-stability SLA of X for the upgrade window". Thoughts @legal-bot?

legal-bot: we can draft appendix language. Need clear definitions: "signed approval token", "cutover window", "egress-stability" metric (e.g., "no more than N IP changes per service per upgrade"), and a force-majeure carveout. Also list required customer responsibilities (provide IPAM API creds if using automatic reservation).

Priya: operational point: include a human-in-loop skip that allows firewall ops to manually approve via the URL, and a machine path for customers with IPAM APIs where we call out to their reservation endpoint. Both must produce the same signed token afterwards.

Victor: CI/QA: add manifest-approve simulation to pipeline. Tests: 1) approval URL used by authorized principal yields token; 2) expired token fails; 3) replayed token rejected; 4) token bound to manifest id. Also test rollback when preflight fails.

security: add KMS integration checklist to launch gates: customer CMK verification, envelope encryption test, audit log delivery, and manual review of key access policy. No manifest export without passing KMS binding test.

Maya: prioritization: Phase A (manifest + approval URL + manual approval workflow + contract appendix) - high priority; Phase B (IPAM webhook automation + confidence score for tenant-nat) - medium; Phase C (agentless passive-proxy upgrades) - backlog. Target Phase A alpha in 4 weeks.

Linh: I'll draft the manifest schema today (fields: service, egress_ips, window_start, window_end, reuse_hint, confidence, contact) and add examples for vpc vs tenant-nat.

Priya: i'll collect two customer sign-off workflows to validate the approval UX.

Victor: i'll spike the approve endpoint + token flow and wire it into installer dry-run.

Maya: great. I'll schedule 30m to review contract appendix and acceptance tests tomorrow 10:30. Please bring one real customer firewall policy or failing case. Closing thread.
